column23: I explain that human conversation is like an interface that we use to exchange ideas between each other, and we create it naturally the same way we naturally learn how to use our bodies to walk. AI agents can also exchange ideas and accomplish goals for humans, but the conversation interface that allows humans and AI agents to communicate with each other must be designed and built, because an AI agent currently cannot create it naturally through learning. Conversation design is a discipline combining linguistics, psychology, data analytics, UX/UI design, and software development that enables the construction of Human–AI conversational interfaces.
column24: As AI agents become more sophisticated, it becomes more important to make their capabilities accessible to all users and customers. If comparing an AI agent that is extremely capable but which requires users to learn code or a complex non-verbal interface to use with an AI agent of the same capacity that users can talk to using the conversational interface they already know in their own language, they will prefer the conversational AI agent.
column25: Conversation design is not scriptwriting or technical writing. While storyboards and flow diagrams are an important part, conversation designers are not building dialogs. column23: To me, conversation design encompasses all aspects of the conversation - whether it's chat, voice, or multimodal. For instance, not only am I creating the persona of how the experience will sound, but I am also thinking through how the UI (if any) will align with that persona, and how the conversation itself can too. It's much more than just what the system says - it's how the system says it, how we provide help to users, and how the entire experience flows from end-to-end.
column24: The business-focused answer is that it can cut down a lot on customer care/assistance resources. An effective chatbot or even IVR can help users feel empowered and resolve their own issues, instead of being dependent on company representatives. When done well, good conversation design can reduce business costs and provide a more efficient experience for the user.

Not necessarily what ISN'T conversation design, but coworkers often assume conversation design is JUST deciding what words/phrasing to have the system use. So often I get requests from product teams for design work and they've already fully built out flows and want me to just create the copy. While that is PART of the job, in my understanding, my job is to be responsible for the end-to-end experience. Often times we have to go in and redo all these flows that were created because the process doesn't make sense to the user, or the team didn't fully think through how the flow will fit into the rest of the experience.

I do think the title of conversation designer often varies a lot from company to company, and based on size and resources, you may be asked to do more than just create conversational experiences.

column23:
Conversation design is a discipline that hybridizes several fields of knowledge, among them linguistics, psychology and computer science.
The goal of conversation design is to design conversational/dialogue flows that enable automated tools able to interact with users in natural language and help resolve the tasks the agent is called to perform.
Conversation design includes a purely humanistic part tied to copywriting (writing and defining the agent's communication style), a part that combines expertise in dialogue management (linguistics/psychology/psycholinguistics) and aims at designing fluid interaction trees, as well as skills related to the underlying technologies and therefore the limits and functionalities that can be exploited in dialogue.
column24: Conversation design makes it possible to build tools that ease user interaction by avoiding conversational loops, handling failure cases, etc. Very often it is useful to clearly represent the company or entity the tool speaks for to the end user. column24:
Conversation design is essential because it improves communication between companies and users, making interactions more natural, efficient and accessible. For companies, this means offering more agile service, reducing operating costs and strengthening customer relationships.

For users, good conversation design makes it easier to access information and services, avoids frustration with slow service and ensures a more fluid and humanized experience.
column25:
Conversation design goes beyond simply drawing chatbot flows or writing automatic replies. It involves creating strategic interactions, always considering the user experience, business goals and usability best practices. The goal is to create efficient and natural communication adapted to the context of each interaction.

A common mistake I see is treating the conversation as a simple automated FAQ, without taking into account tone of voice, the user journey or context. Another frequent problem is creating very rigid dialogues that don't allow flexibility for different ways of responding or the user's real needs.

I also see a lack of accessibility in many chatbots, especially in journeys aimed at specific audiences, such as people aged 60+, who still face difficulties with technology. A good example is bots used in processes such as taking out payroll-deductible loans for retirees, where the solution needs to be accessible, simple and adapted to that audience. Many bots fail at this because they don't consider the characteristics and needs of the target audience.

In addition, it is crucial to dive into the client's business. Each brand needs a customized chatbot architecture, with AI or not. It makes no sense to adopt the same structure for all chatbots, even if they are in the same industry, such as automotive. Each situation requires a strategic adjustment that specifically serves the client and their audience.

Conversation design is designing an optimal experience at the intersection of business viability, technical feasibility and customer desirability.

column23: For me, Conversation Design is about creating natural, intuitive interactions between people and AI systems—whether chatbots, voice assistants, or multimodal experiences. It’s a mix of UX design, linguistics, and AI, where the goal is to make conversations feel smooth and effective. It’s about understanding user needs, designing clear dialogue flows, and balancing business objectives with a great user experience.
column24: Conversation Design is crucial because it bridges the gap between businesses and users, making AI interactions more natural, efficient, and user-friendly. For businesses, well-designed conversations improve customer engagement, streamline support, and enhance brand perception. For users, they reduce frustration, save time, and create more intuitive, human-like interactions. A well-crafted conversational experience benefits both sides by making technology feel more accessible and helpful.
column25: Conversation Design isn’t just about making AI sound human or crafting chatbot scripts—it’s about designing structured, goal-driven interactions that align with business objectives. Many assume it’s just about personality, but the real focus should be on efficiency, clarity, and driving measurable outcomes. A common mistake is prioritizing a friendly tone over functionality, when the real goal is to create seamless experiences that satisfy both user needs and business goals.

column23: Conversation design is the art and science of creating natural, effective, and user-friendly interactions between humans and AI-driven systems, such as chatbots and voice assistants. It blends linguistics, UX design, psychology, and AI technology to craft engaging, context-aware conversations. The goal is to ensure that bots communicate clearly, understand user intent, and guide interactions smoothly, improving overall user experience and business outcomes.
column24:
Conversation design is crucial for both businesses and users because it enhances communication efficiency, user satisfaction, and operational effectiveness.

For businesses, well-designed conversations reduce customer service costs, improve automation rates, and enhance brand perception by delivering smooth, human-like interactions. Thoughtful design also ensures compliance, consistency, and better engagement across digital touchpoints.

For users, it creates intuitive, frictionless experiences, reducing frustration and effort. A well-designed bot understands intent, provides relevant responses, and seamlessly resolves issues, ultimately improving customer satisfaction and trust in the brand.
column25:
Conversation design isn’t just writing chatbot scripts or adding AI to a customer service flow. A common mistake is thinking it’s only about words when, in reality, it’s about structuring interactions for clarity, efficiency, and engagement.

Many assume that AI alone can handle conversations without human design. But without thoughtful intent mapping, error handling, and user-centric design, bots often frustrate users instead of helping them. Conversation design is about guiding AI—not just trusting it to “figure it out.”

1 - Today I see far fewer growth opportunities in the profession than a few years ago. I am disconnected from new opportunities, but talking to people who follow this closely, the perception is that opportunities, scale and growth are shrinking every day. With the mass adoption of generative technologies, this perception is reinforced by the business and its eternal goal of cutting costs and generating profit. My perception is that the use of automated tools to help less qualified people in the field is gaining ground.

2 - I would separate "my work" from the "need for this function" within the company where I work. My work may not have the necessary recognition for 2 reasons:
- Lack of indicators that contribute to this visibility (and when it comes to experience, this metric is much more challenging to measure in the short term)
- Management is business-driven (not experience-driven), so the viewpoint of those managing is never one of Design/conversation design process, but of "profit" and "costs".

In that sense, I don't think my specific work is valued, despite the recognition that undoubtedly exists.

On the other hand, and I believe the question is or should be about this, I understand that the role of conversation designers is well regarded and respected at the institution where I work. And the number of professionals involved, I believe, is above average.

3 - Regarding the last question, being just one among the 45-50 conversation designers at the institution, there is no possibility of my work causing significant impact with scalable solutions. Everything is already highly scaled; I joined when it was already moving. I just follow the established processes (even while identifying the many points of opportunity/problems). Changing something or developing a solution involves much more business and a whole team than my sole intention. And that is slow and almost demotivating in my scenario.

column23: Conversation Design is about how we solve problems intuitively for users interacting with chat and voice experiences. How can we use those experiences to drive satisfaction, solve problems and enhance business processes. It's a bit of a mishmash of UX, Psychology, Copy, and now with a very strong flavour of Prompt Design and Engineering.
column24: So many people are bitter about interacting with bots. I think they have a really negative perception. As a Conversation Designer, my job is to show users they can have really neat, intuitive and fun experiences that actually solved their problems. From a business perspective, Conversation Design has bottom line impact. The better we can design and solve user problems through automation, the better it is for the company. As a Conversation Designer, my role within an organisation is often to advocate for these experiences, and how we can always be pushing the needle. Many organisations are stuck in the dark ages when it comes to assistants, and are only re-emerging now. My job is to show them what is possible, and how it can benefit the business.
column25: Writing FAQs or just sample dialogues. Many content designers or UX writers I speak to say they've done Conversation Design because they're written chatbot scripts. column23:
Conversation design is all about making AI chatbots and voice assistants feel natural, helpful, and easy to talk to. It’s like designing a really good customer service experience—just without a human on the other end. The goal is to make sure the bot understands what people are asking, responds in a way that makes sense, and actually helps them get what they need.

It’s not just about writing replies—it’s about creating a smooth back-and-forth flow, making sure the bot sounds like the brand, and handling things like misunderstandings or weird questions without frustrating the user. A good conversation design keeps people engaged, solves problems fast, and makes automation feel effortless instead of robotic.

At the end of the day, it’s about helping businesses talk to their customers in a way that’s smart, natural, and actually useful
column24:
Conversation design is super useful for business owners because it helps them save time, capture more leads, and provide better customer service—without needing to be available 24/7. Instead of missing out on potential customers or overwhelming their team with repetitive questions, a well-designed AI chatbot can handle inquiries, book appointments, qualify leads, and even follow up automatically.

It also makes businesses look more professional and responsive. Customers expect instant replies, and if a business can provide that—even through automation—it builds trust and keeps people engaged. Plus, AI-driven conversations scale effortlessly, meaning a business can handle hundreds of inquiries at once without hiring extra staff.

Ultimately, conversation design turns chatbots from boring, robotic scripts into smart, engaging tools that actually drive sales, improve customer experience, and free up business owners to focus on what they do best
column25:
One of the biggest mistakes people make about conversation design is thinking it’s just about writing chatbot replies. It’s not just about coming up with responses—it’s about designing a full, natural, and goal-driven conversation that actually helps users get what they need.

Another misconception is that a chatbot should sound overly human. While it’s great for AI to feel natural and friendly, trying too hard to mimic a human can backfire—especially if the bot can’t actually think, understand context deeply, or handle complex requests. The goal isn’t to trick people into thinking they’re talking to a human—it’s to create a smooth, efficient experience that makes interactions easier and faster.

People also assume that chatbots can work perfectly right away without testing. In reality, good conversation design requires iteration—analyzing real interactions, improving responses, and fine-tuning the chatbot based on what users actually need. A poorly designed chatbot that gives generic, unhelpful answers does more harm than good.

At the end of the day, conversation design isn’t just about automating replies—it’s about creating a thoughtful, useful, and seamless experience that makes AI a real asset to a business.

column31: Most purpose-built design tools in conversational AI are development tools, no matter what the purveyors say. What conversation designers need to support a proper design process are lightweight tools that allow them to focus solely on the interaction they're creating. Any tool that forces the user to decide if they want a script node or an entity, for example, before dropping a shape on a page, is by definition forcing that designer away from the interaction and into the technology. To be clear: designs have to represent interactions that the technology can support, but you don't achieve that by introducing technical decisions in at the earliest design phase.

The conversation designer position needs to be positioned from another perspective. It is no longer just someone who designs a flow, but a key profile for the business. To achieve this, these profiles must be trained in topics such as data analysis and metrics, or even basic technical topics.

column23: Conversation design is the discipline/practice of ensuring that the interaction between a human and a nonhuman system in a conversational, language-based interface is as accessible, easy, efficient, useful, credible, and intelligent as possible.
column24: Conversation design, when done well, ensures that a user-facing conversational interface/product is beneficial to human users and, by extension, the businesses to which the conversational product belongs. Conversational products are usually deployed by businesses with the goal of increasing revenue and/or decreasing costs. But the quality of the user experience (and how much it is improved over however users previously dealt with the task in question) is fundamental. If the conversational experience is worse than whatever preceded it, users won't adopt it at scale; perhaps they'll try it once or twice before giving up on it and forgetting it. The underlying technology can be as advanced as we'd like, but, in order for the conversational product to "move the needle" and have any significant business impact, users must use it and come back to use it over and over again. This requires a tremendous amount of investigation, planning, dialogue, coordination, design sense, and technical know-how. The best conversation designers are naturally inquisitive, research-inclined, design-minded, collaborative, tech savvy, and fierce advocates for human end users.
column25: Conversation focuses on the content and the sequence of the interaction between a human user and a nonhuman system. Conversation design isn't coding. It isn't graphic design. And while it is deeply interdependent on language models (LLM, NLU, directed dialog, whatever), it isn't just linguists.

Action to achieve a 5:
- Educate clients on the impact of good conversation design through case studies and measurable outcomes.
- Advocate for early involvement in decision-making processes to ensure the design is not treated as an afterthought.
- Work closely with stakeholders to align expectations and showcase the business value of a well-designed conversational experience.

3)
The current client lacks the necessary maturity in conversation design, which may lead to resistance to implementing scalable solutions. This can result in more tactical, short-term work rather than meaningful, long-lasting impact.

Actions to Achieve a 5:
Help the client build a roadmap for conversational AI maturity, showing incremental steps toward automation and improvement.
Offer workshops or training to educate them on best practices, frameworks, and long-term strategies.
Encourage experimentation with MVPs (Minimum Viable Products) to demonstrate the value of scalable solutions without overwhelming them.

column25:
Conversation design has a lot of powerful tools - entities, intents, LLMs, and words.  However, conversation design is not just any one of those tools.  For example, an LLM can have a conversation with something, but that doesn't mean it's a good conversation.  Words are predictable, but users responses to them are not necessarily predictable.  Conversation design is about understanding the choices, possibilities, and tradeoffs when attempting to solve a problem with a conversational interface.

Also, conversation design is not a one-off thing.  It requires careful monitoring and iteration to improve the effectiveness of the conversational experiences for users and new cases.

column24: Conversation design is fundamental because it improves the user experience and business efficiency. column25: Conversation design is the art and science of designing interactions between humans and machines through natural language, both text and voice. It is not just about writing answers for chatbots or voice assistants, but about creating fluid, useful and intuitive experiences, respecting the dynamics of a natural conversation. Many people think it is only a matter of writing, or that integrating a chatbot is enough to have good design. In reality, it is a complex process involving UX design, artificial intelligence, linguistics, psychology and data analysis. Good conversation design is not limited to responding but anticipates needs, handles errors and guides the user naturally and without frustration.

Overall, Conversation Design is a specialized field within user experience (UX) design that focuses on crafting interactions between humans and conversational interfaces, such as (but not limited to) chatbots, voice assistants, and virtual agents. 

In my work, I combine my knowledge of UX design, psychology, content design, brand development, and marketing to inform the conversations between a user and a digital system to ensure interactions are intuitive, helpful, and engaging.
column24: Conversation design is crucial in an era where digital assistants and chatbots are becoming primary interfaces for many digital services, aiming to mimic human-to-human interaction as closely as possible to enhance user engagement and satisfaction. column25: Conversation design is not one singular role or a single person trying to do multiple roles associated with the pieces of conversation design. The biggest challenge is being heard above all the noise that is being generated around AI. There's a lot of inexperienced and self-proclaimed experts who are trying to get a piece of the "AI pie" who are great at getting attention and clients but aren't delivering on their promises or work.  There's a lot of big consultancies who claim expertise but truly don't have a foundation of knowledge. The result is a knock on the credibility and value of conversational AI that means the genuine practitioners and experts have a bigger uphill climb because of a negative perception that often isn't warranted. 

We also have to figure out how to stop allowing the software/technology side of things drive awareness and evangelization because often those products present creating chatbots as "fast and easy" and truthfully, good experiences require time, resources, and knowledge so they aren't fast and easy. The result is a lot of organizations creating bad experiences that could have been avoided.

column23:
Conversation design is the process of crafting natural interactions between humans and technology based on user needs. Conversation designers teach AI systems how to process, understand, and respond to human language in real-time, simulating human-like conversation. 

What it is:
- Understanding user needs and how to advocate for them and tying them together with business needs
- Asking clarifying questions to understand requirements and what needs to be communicated to users
- Knowing how to communicate well and work well with all the different types of stakeholders you mentioned above on highly cross-functional teams 
- Thinking through everything that could happen in order to design seamless experiences and mitigate any harm that could come to people
- Analyzing research, conversations, and data and analytics in order to improve conversational AI experiences 
- Training AI models and systems
- Staying on top of the latest conversational AI technologies

1. Just writing words. People think conversation design is just about crafting conversations, but it is so much more than that in terms of understanding user needs, working with cross-functional teams, helping define business goals, understanding how all the technical pieces need to fit together and how that impacts the experience, and all the other parts of the job that are more invisible. 

2. A one and done thing. Companies often think they can just release a chatbot or conversational experience and they don't need to do anything else, but they don't realize the work is only beginning when the experience is launched. There needs to be constant monitoring and iterations to make sure people are still getting what they need out of the experience and to identify any gaps and opportunities to make the experience better.

column23:
Conversation design is a multidisciplinary field that crafts intuitive and human-like interactions between users and AI systems. It replicates the principles of natural human conversation to create seamless and engaging dialogues with digital platforms like chatbots and voice assistants. 

This discipline combines UX, linguistics, and AI to ensure natural, clear, and contextually appropriate interactions, enhancing user experience and customer satisfaction. It involves designing conversational flows, defining voice and tone, and conducting user research to refine interactions.
column24:
Conversation design is crucial for businesses and users because it enhances customer satisfaction and engagement by creating natural, empathetic, personalized interactions with AI systems. It improves efficiency, reduces costs, and fosters stronger customer relationships.

It provides users with a seamless and intuitive experience, making technology more accessible and enjoyable. Businesses can increase customer loyalty and retention by aligning conversational AI with user needs and preferences.
column25:
Conversation design is often misunderstood as being solely about speech recognition or voice interactions, which is incorrect. It encompasses various interactions, including text-based and multimodal experiences across multiple platforms. 

Another misconception is that conversation design only involves pre-programming answers to common questions, overlooking the complexity and nuance of human communication. Many mistakenly believe it’s just about AI when effective designs often rely on more straightforward, rule-based systems.

1. Prototyping: Allows me to visualize and test conversational flows, ensuring user-centered designs that meet real-world needs.

2. Flow Diagramming: Helps in mapping out complex conversational paths, making it easier to identify potential issues and optimize interactions.

3. Data Analysis and Performance Tracking: Enables me to assess how users interact with systems, identify pain points, and make data-driven improvements.

4. Project Management: Keeps projects organized and on track, ensuring timely delivery and effective team collaboration.

5. Version Control and Documentation: Maintains a clear record of changes and updates, ensuring consistency and facilitating collaboration across teams.

In 2024, one of the biggest challenges faced by conversation designers was likely the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into conversational systems. This integration often resulted in a loss of fine-grained control over design, as LLMs can produce responses that do not align with the brand’s voice or context. 

Additionally, ensuring that chatbots can understand complex user queries and provide contextual responses while maintaining a natural flow was a significant challenge. Balancing flexibility with control in AI-driven conversations was also a key issue.
column41:
Reflecting on 2024, I was excited about the trend toward AI agents that offer more fluid and human-like interactions, enhancing conversational experiences beyond traditional chatbots. 

Another exciting development was the integration of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML), which improved AI’s ability to understand human language.

However, I was concerned about ethical considerations, such as biases in AI systems and the potential for harm if not carefully monitored. Additionally, the complexity of human language and the need for AI to handle nuanced inputs effectively remained a significant challenge.

column23:
Conversation Design is the discipline of crafting effective, engaging, and natural interactions between humans and AI-driven conversational interfaces, such as chatbots and voice assistants. It involves a blend of user experience (UX) design, linguistics, psychology, and AI technology to ensure conversations feel intuitive and human-like.

At its core, conversation design focuses on:
	1.	Understanding User Needs – Researching user behavior, pain points, and expectations to design meaningful conversations.
	2.	Defining Bot Persona & Tone – Crafting a bot’s personality, tone, and style to align with brand identity and user demographics.
	3.	Structuring Dialogue Flows – Designing conversation paths that guide users smoothly toward their goals while handling errors and ambiguity effectively.
	4.	Applying Linguistic Principles – Using natural language principles to ensure clarity, coherence, and engagement in responses.
	5.	Ensuring Inclusivity & Accessibility – Designing conversations that accommodate diverse user needs, including different languages, accents, and accessibility requirements.
	6.	Leveraging AI & NLP – Understanding how Natural Language Processing (NLP) works to create training data, intents, and entities that enhance bot understanding.
	7.	Testing & Iteration – Continuously refining the conversation based on user feedback, analytics, and A/B testing.

Good conversation design minimizes friction, reduces user frustration, and enhances engagement, ultimately leading to higher satisfaction and improved business outcomes.

column40:
The biggest challenge faced by conversation designers in 2024 was balancing Generative AI capabilities with structured, reliable user experiences. While GenAI offered unprecedented flexibility in handling open-ended conversations, it also introduced new hurdles:
	1.	Control vs. Creativity – Traditional intent-based chatbots relied on structured flows, ensuring predictable and reliable interactions. With GenAI, responses became more dynamic, but designers had to ensure they remained accurate, on-brand, and aligned with business goals without veering into hallucinations.
	2.	Maintaining Consistency in Persona & Tone – GenAI models could generate varied responses, making it challenging to maintain consistent bot personality, tone, and style across conversations. Designers had to fine-tune prompts, create guardrails, and implement style guidelines to ensure the bot stayed true to its intended voice.
	3.	Reducing Hallucinations & Misinformation – Unlike traditional bots that followed predefined scripts, GenAI often fabricated responses when uncertain. Conversation designers had to find ways to limit hallucinations using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), controlled prompt engineering, and fallback strategies.
	4.	Ensuring Ethical & Responsible AI Use – With increasing scrutiny on AI biases and misinformation, designers had to be proactive in removing biases, ensuring fairness, and making AI interactions transparent. This included handling sensitive topics, data privacy, and regulatory compliance.
	5.	Seamless Handovers & Escalations – Many enterprises still relied on hybrid AI-human support models. Designers had to ensure smooth transitions between AI and live agents while maintaining context and reducing user frustration.
	6.	Scalability Across Channels – As users interacted with bots on multiple platforms (chat, voice, social media, etc.), designers had to create adaptable conversation flows that worked across modalities while optimizing for platform-specific nuances.
	7.	Redefining Metrics & Success Criteria – Traditional chatbot KPIs (containment rate, intent accuracy, etc.) needed to be re-evaluated in GenAI-driven bots. Designers had to establish new measurement frameworks to assess effectiveness beyond containment, focusing on engagement, relevance, and user satisfaction.

In short, 2024 was the year when conversation designers had to evolve from scripting rigid bot dialogues to orchestrating flexible, yet controlled AI interactions—leveraging the power of GenAI while mitigating its risks.
column41:
Most Exciting Trends in Conversation Design (2024)
	1.	Mainstream Adoption of Generative AI in Conversational Interfaces
– The rise of GenAI-powered chatbots transformed conversation design from rigid intent-based flows to more fluid, contextual, and open-ended interactions.
– Designers gained new tools to dynamically generate responses, leading to more personalized and engaging user experiences.
	2.	Conversational Agents Becoming Multi-Modal
– The integration of text, voice, images, and even video into AI interactions made bots more versatile.
– AI assistants could now analyze documents, screenshots, and voice inputs to provide more intelligent and contextual responses.
	3.	Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for More Reliable AI Responses
– Instead of relying purely on model-generated responses, many companies adopted RAG techniques, ensuring bots pulled from verified sources and up-to-date knowledge bases.
– This helped reduce hallucinations while keeping responses dynamic.
	4.	Personalization & Context Awareness at Scale
– AI-driven chatbots became more personalized by remembering user history, preferences, and past interactions.
– Context retention across conversations helped create a more human-like and intuitive experience.
	5.	Enterprise Investment in AI Copilots & Assistive AI
– Businesses moved beyond basic chatbots to AI copilots that assisted employees in real-time decision-making.
– AI-powered customer service assistants helped human agents by providing real-time suggestions, summarizing conversations, and automating repetitive tasks.

Most Concerning Trends in Conversation Design (2024)
	1.	Unpredictability & Hallucinations in Generative AI Responses
– AI-generated responses weren’t always reliable, often fabricating information when knowledge gaps existed.
– Designers had to spend more time defining guardrails and testing edge cases to prevent misleading information.
	2.	Loss of Control Over Brand Voice & Persona Consistency
– While GenAI allowed for flexibility in responses, it also made persona consistency a challenge.
– Companies struggled to keep AI outputs aligned with brand identity, leading to unpredictable tone and style mismatches.
	3.	Increased Ethical & Privacy Concerns
– With more AI assistants collecting user data for personalization, concerns around data privacy, security, and compliance became more critical.
– Regulators began pushing for stricter AI governance, making designers more accountable for bias mitigation and responsible AI usage.
	4.	Struggles with Hybrid AI-Human Interactions
– While AI became more advanced, seamless handovers to human agents still faced friction.
– Many businesses underestimated the importance of a well-designed escalation process, frustrating users when AI failed to resolve complex issues.
	5.	Metrics & Success Measurement Lagging Behind AI Evolution
– Traditional chatbot success metrics (containment rate, intent accuracy, etc.) didn’t fully capture the effectiveness of GenAI-driven bots.
– Companies struggled to define new KPIs that measured the quality of conversations beyond automation rates.

Final Thoughts

2024 was a transformative year for conversation design—one where the discipline expanded beyond pre-scripted flows to more dynamic, AI-driven interactions. While GenAI unlocked new creative possibilities, it also introduced challenges around control, reliability, and ethics.

Going forward, conversation designers will need to master AI orchestration—balancing the flexibility of GenAI with structured guardrails and human oversight to create trustworthy, engaging, and effective AI interactions.

column23: Conversation design is the discipline in charge of creating natural interaction experiences between people and systems, such as chatbots or virtual assistants. It combines UX, language, technology and strategy to design flows, personalities and responses that not only solve needs but do so in a human, clear and efficient way, integrating LLMs, data analysis and strategic design to achieve contextualized, high-impact conversational experiences.
column24: Conversation design is key because it connects people with companies in a direct, natural and efficient way. For users, it means getting clear, fast and human answers without navigating complex processes. For companies, it represents an opportunity to scale service, improve customer experience, strengthen the brand and generate value (in conversions, retention or satisfaction). Applied strategically, it optimizes products, reduces friction and aligns technology with the real needs of the business and people.
column25:
In my opinion, conversation design is not just writing nice dialogues or "talking like a bot". Nor is it simply slapping a friendly copy on an automated interface. Many people confuse it with just UX writing or with technical development, when in reality it is a strategic practice that involves research, experience design, personality definition, conversational logic, and deep understanding of the context of use.

A common mistake is thinking that any chatbot is the result of conversation design. But if there is no intention behind it, if it wasn't designed with the user, their language, emotions and goals in mind, it is not design: it is just automation.

I see an increasingly widespread perception, among makers of AI platforms, that their products are so sophisticated that conversation design and its purveyors are no longer necessary or relevant. Our presence implies that their products are not inherently PERFECT, and they deem this implication unacceptable. As a result, CD is treated as "optional at best", much like sprinkles on top a cupcake: to be added at the last minute, purely as decoration to the "real" treat: the AI-generated framework that is the cupcake.

The truth, of course, is that skilled CD is more critical than ever, in this Age of AI. But that is not the perception, which is resulting in a steady erosion of both our compensation and our reputation.

column23: Conversation design creates natural, user-centered interactions between people and technology, like chatbots and voice assistants. It blends UX design, linguistics, and AI to craft intuitive dialogue flows, recognize user intent, and ensure smooth error handling. By defining a brand’s tone and personality, conversation design enhances engagement, reduces friction, and improves customer satisfaction, ultimately shaping positive brand experiences.
column24: Conversation design is crucial for businesses because it enhances customer satisfaction, reduces operational costs, and strengthens brand perception by delivering seamless, efficient, and engaging interactions. For users, it provides intuitive, personalized experiences that minimize frustration, save time, and help them achieve their goals effortlessly. Well-designed conversations build trust, foster loyalty, and ensure that technology serves as a helpful, human-like extension of the brand.
column25: Conversation design isn’t just writing chatbot scripts or clever prompts — it’s a strategic process that blends UX, linguistics, and AI to create seamless, intuitive interactions. The biggest misconception is that “anyone who can write can do conversation design,” but without understanding user intent, error management, and system behavior, even the best-written responses will lead to frustrating experiences. Great conversation design is about designing how a system responds, not just what it says.
